newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT - DePuy poised for solid debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT - DePuy poised for solid debut.

text.p: DePuy Inc's established reputation as a maker of orthopedic devices and its sound fundamentals should offer investors a good long-term buying opportunity at its initial public offering this week.

"It will garner the attention of institutional players and those not looking for a quick fix but an investment," said David Menlow, president of Springfield, N.J.- based IPO Financial Network Corp. "We like it because of who they are and who's doing the deal. Morgan Stanley is not going to take in a deal this size and have it be a non-event."

DePuy -- whose core products are reconstructive implant devices for hips and knees -- is offering 14.78 million shares at an estimated price range of $16.50 to $18.50 in a deal led by Morgan Stanley & Co.
"We're seeing a premium of maybe about one point at the opening," said Vincent Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald. "Something this big won't see an opening much higher."
Peggy Farley, chief executive of Amas Securities, likes the deal "very much." "It (DePuy) has a long history of profitability, and its (main) products have been around a long time," she said.
The company, which was founded in 1895, recorded net sales of $636.6 million in 1995, up from $551.8 million in 1994 and $466.7 million in 1993.

Ryan Jacob, director of research at IPO Value Monitor, sees the company continuing to grow at a respectable pace. "We see revenue growth at around 15 percent annually, and earnings growth at around 20 percent," he said.

DePuy, along with other medical device makers, is adapting to a rapidly changing health care environment in the United States. With the emergence of managed care, and the pressure to restrain costs mounting within the industry, DePuy is making more discounted bulk sales to large outfits like hospital groups. This means, said Jacob,"lower gross margins, but (this) is offset by higher volumes."

Other orthopedic device manufacturers, like Biomet Inc, have chosen a different strategy. "DePuy is competing on price strategy, whereas Biomet competes on service and product attributes," said David Lebedeff, analyst at NatCity Investments.

The industry has also seen legal costs from patent infringement suits and product liability claims rising in recent years. Biomet said last month that it saw as unavoidable an escalation in defense and settlement costs in the current legal environment.
However, analysts say, this trend goes with the territory, and is not greatly worrying for strong companies. Overall, "the long-term outlook (for the industry) is very favorable," said Lebedeff.

DePuy intends to use the proceeds of the offering primarily for the expansion of its business through acquisitions, according to its prospectus. Earlier this year, the company bought Orthopedic Technology Inc for $46.2 million.
The stock is being offered by both DePuy and Corange Ltd, the holding company of Boehringer Mannheim GmbH, the European pharmaceutical, chemicals and diagnostics company.
According to the prospectus, Corange and its subsidiaries will own about 84.8 percent of DePuy's common stock after the IPO.
